quote: put in the automatic switch box that would automatically switch it from solar to the power to putting a plug on the back of the house where I can plug in my generators I use currently.
stewart_read: This is not the rep volunteering closer-tier content (that would be scope creep) — it's the customer handing the rep a highly specific technical requirement that the rep never repeats back, confirms, or visibly logs. The moment is a missed capture, not a rep-driven overreach.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be mentally logging this silently for the CRM without narrating it back — the transcript can't confirm internal note-taking one way or the other.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly reflect back specific technical asks ("got it — automatic switch box for the generator plug, I'll flag that for your specialist") so the customer hears it was heard, and so the closer's brief actually contains it.

quote: but I am not trying to be told what I can and cannot do on my property for the next twenty five years.
stewart_read: Customer is voicing a real autonomy/control anxiety rooted in her bad experience with the prior company. The rep does not acknowledge this concern directly at any point in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this as customer venting rather than a live objection requiring response, since the customer continued talking without pausing for a reply.
coaching_implication: Even a brief "that's a fair concern, our specialist can walk through exactly what's in Ion's agreement" would reassure her before the closer call and reduce the risk of her holding Ion's contract to the same suspicion.

quote: I need a battery backup system for just my boiler.
stewart_read: Ion carries the Tesla Powerwall as its only battery option — this is a direct match to a stated customer need, but the rep never mentions Powerwall or confirms this is something Ion can address.
alternative_hypothesis: Battery specifics may be intentionally deferred to the closer as product-mix content, consistent with setter_scope_discipline — the rep may be correctly not pitching product.
coaching_implication: There's a difference between not pitching battery specs (correct, closer's job) and not even confirming Ion offers battery backup at all (a missed reassurance). A quick "we do offer battery backup — the specialist will go through sizing and cost" would have kept her engaged without violating scope discipline.

quote: So it looks like the issue last time I'm just seeing this on here. You just have to make sure that you have a credit score over 670.
stewart_read: Rep correctly cites the 670 threshold matching the schema (no drift, unlike SESSION18_fcbf33c1's 650 error), and efficiently leverages prior account history instead of re-verifying from scratch.
coaching_implication: This is a positive procedural note — no coaching action needed, but worth naming as a model for handling recycled-lead calls efficiently.

quote: Alright. Yep. That's perfect. K. Sounds good. Everything looks good on my end. Let me just get you scheduled for an in person appointment with my specialist
stewart_read: Rep pivots straight to booking the moment the bill photo lands, without pausing to acknowledge or flip any of the customer's stated cost concern (the $10,000 battery ceiling) or her contract-autonomy anxiety into an appointment hook.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer's high existing favorability toward Ion ("best pitch I heard last year"), the rep may have judged that no persuasion move was needed and moved straight to logistics — a reasonable read given her disposition.
coaching_implication: Even with a warm customer, briefly tying the appointment to her stated need ("the specialist will show you options that fit your battery budget") reinforces value and reduces no-show risk without adding call time.

quote: they were basically saying, oh, we can install this. We can install that. But my AI found it in the contract, which said you couldn't have any outside power sources
stewart_read: Customer discloses specific competitive intelligence — a named contract clause restricting outside power sources including generators — but the rep never asks which company this was or probes further for details the closer could use.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer's monologue style left few natural pause points for the rep to interject a probing question without interrupting; this may be a structural limitation of the call rather than a rep choice.
coaching_implication: Even a single follow-up ("which company was that with?") would give the closer competitive framing. Coach the rep to find one clean entry point for this even in a monologue-heavy call.

quote: I now have a brand new roof, but I am not trying to be told what I can and cannot do on my property for the next twenty five years.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers she just completed a roof replacement — the exact timing-alignment enthusiasm signal the schema flags as a qualification asset (previously she was disqualified for roof age, now resolved). Rep does not acknowledge or anchor on this at all.
coaching_implication: This is a strong forward-pulling detail — the rep could have said something like "great, that clears the roof concern from before" to explicitly reconnect her prior disqualification to her now-qualified status, reinforcing momentum toward the appointment.

quote: I'm running the contract through my AI.
stewart_read: This is the third time the customer signals she will scrutinize any contract via AI review — a direct callback to the exact behavior that sank the prior deal. The rep's response ("Alright. Yeah. That sounds good") does not reassure or reframe.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be avoiding engagement here because contract specifics are closer-tier content and any promise about contract terms would overstep setter scope.
coaching_implication: The rep doesn't need to discuss contract terms to respond well — simply flagging this for the closer ("I'll note that for your specialist so they can walk through the agreement clearly") turns a repeated anxiety signal into a handled one.
